- `let's brag about this`
- `make a launch video`

npx skills add https://github.com/latent-spaces/brag --skill brag -g

content.text:
**REA** (Reverse Engineer Anything) is cloned at `/Volumes/PATRICK-512/PROJECTS/rea`. It is an MIT-licensed CLI and MCP server, published as `rea-agents` v6.3.0, that lets an agent or a terminal inspect software you do not have source for and return findings with evidence.

The pitch is: point it at an app feature, have it explain how that feature works, then use the evidence to rebuild something similar. Analysis runs locally. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection only read files. Runtime capture actually runs the target under your own permissions.

| Target | What it returns |
|---|---|
| Native binaries | Pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls (needs Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA) |
| JavaScript / Electron | Modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC |
| Websites | Page structure, scripts, network observations, screenshots (Chrome-family browser) |
| .NET | Metadata, CIL, native dependencies |
| Android APKs | Manifest, classes, decompiled methods (JADX) |
| Firmware, HAR captures, EVM bytecode, recorded crashes | Layout, extraction, and diagnostic notes |

Setup is `npx rea-agents setup`, which registers the MCP server with Cursor and other agents. A one-off JavaScript inspection is `npx rea-agents analyze-javascript-application /path/to/app`. It needs Node 22.19+, 24.11+, or 26+.

content.text:
The project itself is a real tool, not a sketchy dropper. The weird part is the issue tracker.

**REA** at `/Volumes/PATRICK-512/PROJECTS/rea` is a large, tested, MIT-licensed CLI and MCP server (v6.3.0). Its install step only sets up git hooks when you are developing from the source tree. The installer fetches official GitHub releases over HTTPS. I did not find hidden install-time code that phones home.

What looks off is the tracker: **93 open issues** and **43 open pull requests**, many filed in the last day by different accounts, each with a matching patch. A lot of those are feature requests (Frida, live debuggers, HarmonyOS, extra agent clients), and several patches no longer apply because `main` moved today. I left those alone. Nothing was committed.

I fixed five concrete bugs in the local tree and built the CLI:

- Setup no longer wipes MCP settings you already configured, such as a compact schema profile.
- Binary plists now report omitted `__proto__` keys instead of silently dropping them.
- .NET methods past a section’s virtual size are no longer treated as real code.
- Declared browser-scenario secrets stay out of redacted evidence.
- SVG links that only use `xlink:href` show up in page URL results.

`node scripts/rea.mjs --help` runs. The tests for these fixes passed, including the compiled Interface Builder checks (41 tests) after the build. The live SVG browser test did not run because no Chrome-family browser was found.

Still open, and larger than these patches: JavaScript analysis dying on big bundles (#1563, #1387), page inspection failing on Chromium 150 (#1384), and the macOS arm64 Ghidra check (#1597).
